item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 122307
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Mon Oct 12 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located within a hundred miles west of Cabo Corrientes,
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico (EP93):
Showers and thunderstorms are beginning to show signs of
organization in association with a broad area of low pressure
located several hundred miles south-southwest of the coast of
Guatemala. This system is gradually becoming better defined, and
environmental conditions are forecast to be conducive for further
development. A tropical depression or tropical storm is expected to
form well south of southern Mexico later tonight or tomorrow while
the system moves generally west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...near 100 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...near 100 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 22a
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
542 
WTPZ35 KNHC 122333
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Intermediate Advisory Number 22A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
500 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
...SIMON EXPECTED TO TURN TO THE NORTHWEST THIS EVENING...
...FLOODING RAINS TO CONTINUE ALONG THE COAST OF WEST-CENTRAL
MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM MST...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.3N 106.9W
ABOUT 80 MI...125 KM W OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 205 MI...325 KM S OF MAZATLAN MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...969 MB...28.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in west-central Mexico should continue to
monitor as changes to watches and warnings are possible later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM MST (0000 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 20.3 North, longitude 106.9 West. Simon is moving
toward the west-northwest near 3 mph (6 km/h). A turn to the 
northwest is expected to occur later tonight, followed by a turn to 
the northeast shortly thereafter. On the forecast track, Simon is
expected to be near Las Islas Marias tonight into Tuesday, and then
approach the west-central Mexico coastline Wednesday and Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Weakening is forecast over the next day or so, but Simon 
could re-intensify some by Wednesday and is forecast to remain a 
hurricane through midweek. Rapid weakening is likely after Simon 
moves inland late this week.
 
Simon is a compact system. Hurricane-force winds extend outward up 
to 10 miles (20 km) from the center and tropical-storm-force winds 
extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 969 mb (28.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are likely to occur in Las Islas Marias 
beginning tonight into Tuesday. Hurricane conditions are possible 
within the watch area on Wednesday, with tropical storm conditions 
possible by Tuesday night.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 5 to 10
inches across coastal west-central Mexico with isolated maximum
amounts of 15 inches over the state of Sinaloa by Thursday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is possible along the immediate
coast near Las Islas Marias. Near the coast, the surge will be
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 122053
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
This afternoon, Simon is a small hurricane that is dealing with some
easterly vertical wind shear. The inner-core continues to produce a
lot of lightning but mostly in the eastern semicircle. The most
recent microwave image was a 1718 UTC AWS pass that also showed this
core asymmetry with the eyewall open on the northwest side on the
180 GHz channel. While the latest 18 UTC subjective Dvorak estimate
remains at CI 5.5/102-kt, the objective intensity estimates from
UW-CIMSS continue to gradually decrease. Thus, the initial intensity
is being reduced to a somewhat uncertain 85 kt this advisory, which
also matches the D-MINT mean estimate from the AWS microwave pass
above. A helpful 1712 UTC Metop-C scatterometer pass was useful to
help adjust Simon's radii and also to indicate its wind field has
become quite small, with 34-kt winds only extending out about     
40 n mi.

Simon's track has thrown us a few curve balls over the past 24-36 h, 
and this afternoon is no exception as the hurricane made a brief 
westward jog, with the longer-term motion estimated at 290/3 kt. The 
track forecast remains problematic. Part of the slow motion Simon is 
exhibiting today is related to competing steering synoptic features, 
primarily a mid-level ridge centered near the Texas Coast versus 
another mid-level ridge located southwest of the hurricane. The 
influence of the northeastern ridge has been a little stronger, but 
steering diagnostics suggest that Simon may be soon reaching a 
bifurcation or COL point in the flow. This feature indicates the 
area where the net steering flow collapses and helps explain why 
both the deterministic and ensemble track guidance spread increases 
quite dramatically in 24 to 48 h. For example, the HAFS-A/B models, 
which earlier this morning were showing a faster northeastward turn 
back into Mexico, now show Simon stalling and executing a slow 
cyclonic loop in the waters between mainland Mexico and the southern 
tip of the Baja California Peninsula. The European ensemble spread 
suggests that these individual solutions are likely just different 
flavors of the overall distribution, which is spread out in a 
southwest to northeast fashion. While the overall track guidance 
continues to have large spread, there has been a northward and 
faster shift this cycle. This shift is a bit odd given the current 
storm motion, so the NHC track forecast is initially on the left 
side of the guidance over the first 12-24 h, but falls back closer 
to the middle of the guidance envelope, and attempts to blend the 
latest HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA), Google Deepmind 
ensemble mean (GDMI), and their latest Weather Next model (WN3I). 
Ultimately the latest track forecast converges close to the prior 
one near landfall in Mexico in 72-96 h, but this remains a low 
confidence track forecast.
 
The intensity forecast for Simon is also challenging. The current
mid-level easterly shear affecting Simon's inner core structure has
not been well anticipated by the model guidance. Small tropical
cyclones like Simon are often more sensitive to negative
environmental factors, and even 15-20 kt of easterly shear could be
enough to disrupt the core structure, especially with nearby
environmental dry air. The factors may result in additional
weakening in the short-term. However, EC-SHIPS guidance shows the
shear lowering below 5 kt in 24-48 h. Assuming Simon is able to
maintain an inner core structure and take advantage of the more
favorable conditions, restrengthening is still forecast, especially
as the hurricane is expected to track over the warmest sea-surface
temperatures in the Eastern Pacific basin (31-32 C). The intensity
guidance shows more short-term weakening compared to the previous
cycle, and the NHC intensity forecast is lower early on, but still
shows restrengthening as Simon encounters those more favorable
conditions, and ends up on the high end of the intensity guidance in
60-72 h. Small storms like Simon can also be prone to rapid changes
in intensity, which continues to make this intensity forecast also
more uncertain than usual. Rapid weakening is still anticipated when
Simon eventually makes landfall in the latter part of this week
between 72-96 h.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Hurricane conditions are likely on Las Islas Marias over the
next day or so, where a Hurricane Warning remains in effect.
 
2. Simon is expected to approach the coast of western Mexico later
this week, where hurricane conditions are possible. A Hurricane
Watch is in effect from Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
west-central Mexico over the next few days. This rainfall will
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
of steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells will affect portions of the southwestern and
west-central coasts of Mexico over the next few days. These swells
are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  12/2100Z 20.2N 106.8W   85 KT 100 MPH
 12H  13/0600Z 20.5N 107.0W   75 KT  85 MPH
 24H  13/1800Z 20.9N 107.5W   65 KT  75 MPH
 36H  14/0600Z 21.2N 107.7W   70 KT  80 MPH
 48H  14/1800Z 21.5N 107.7W   75 KT  85 MPH
 60H  15/0600Z 22.2N 107.4W   80 KT  90 MPH
 72H  15/1800Z 23.0N 107.0W   85 KT 100 MPH
 96H  16/1800Z 24.2N 106.6W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
120H  17/1800Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Papin
